issues.source_quote: Опять Тимофеев пробки пережег! - Товарищ Тимофеев, когда это кончится?
issues.translation_quote: Timofeev has blown the fuses again! - Comrade Timofeev, when will this end?
issues.justification: The 'когда это кончится / когда кончатся ваши опыты' play on 'кончится' is fine, but the later exchange is adequately rendered; however 'Сейчас заканчиваю' answered by 'Я спрашиваю, когда кончатся ваши опыты' loses the quibble on 'end/finish' only partially. (low confidence)

issues.source_quote: У меня сегодня в кафе увели перчатки. И я полюбила другого.
issues.translation_quote: Someone stole my gloves at the café today. And I've fallen in love with another man.
issues.justification: Fine in meaning, but the comic non-sequitur is kept; no issue. (retracted)

issues.translation_quote: Vague doubts haunt me.
issues.justification: The famous quoted line ('Меня терзают смутные сомнения') is a deliberate cultural reference; the rendering loses the literary/mock-heroic echo, and the tense shift to 'haunt' flattens the joke.

issues.source_quote: Не вели казнить, Великий государь, надежа!
issues.translation_quote: Order me not executed, great sovereign, our hope!
issues.justification: Unnatural, calque-like rendering of a fixed formula of petition; 'Spare me, great sovereign' or 'Do not have me executed' would be natural. Repeated many times, damaging the period comic effect.

issues.translation_quote: Shoot, shoot, score...
issues.justification: The hockey chant ('Puck, puck!') is a Soviet cultural joke on the crowd shouting 'Царя, царя'; the translation loses the specific allusion and the parallel.

issues.source_quote: Был у нас толмач немчин. Ему переводить, а он лыка не вяжет. - Мы его в кипятке и сварили.
issues.translation_quote: We had a German interpreter. He was supposed to translate, but he was dead drunk. - So we boiled him in boiling water.
issues.justification: 'Boiled him in boiling water' is redundant and loses the archaic voice; the tone of the courtiers is also modernized ('dead drunk').

issues.source_quote: Дер гроссер кениг, дас шведишен кенигсрейх, зандте мих. Зайнен трейен динер, цу имен, цар и фелики кнезе Иван Василевич Усарусса
issues.translation_quote: Der grosser König, das schwedischen Königreich, sandte mich. Seinen treuen Diener, zu Ihnen, Tsar und Veliki Knyaz Ivan Vasilievich of all Russia
issues.justification: The deliberately garbled phonetic German is 'corrected' into proper German, losing the comic mangling, and the ending is arbitrarily switched into English.

issues.translation_quote: The foreign tourist speaks well!
issues.justification: 'Интурист' refers to the Soviet agency for foreign tourists; the joke is Bunsha treating the ambassador as a tourist, but the rendering is weak and unnatural.

issues.translation_quote: Shpak I did not take.
issues.justification: Earlier 'Квартиру Шпака Вы брали?' was translated 'Did you hit Shpak's apartment?', which loses the pun on 'брать' (take city / burgle) that drives the joke; the wording 'hit' undermines the Kazan/Astrakhan parallel.

issues.source_quote: Ваше сиятельство, смилуйтесь... Языками не владею, Ваше благородие.
issues.translation_quote: Your Excellency, have mercy.
issues.justification: Zhorzh's ranks and Bunsha's failed attempt at Slavonic are fine, but 'Паки, паки... Иже херувимы!' rendering as transliteration is acceptable; however 'Языками не владею' becomes 'I don't speak languages', losing the pun on 'языки' (languages/tongues).

issues.translation_quote: Boor!
issues.justification: Archaic, stilted word for a modern angry retort; 'Boor' sounds out of place in a contemporary 1970s setting.

issues.translation_quote: Don't close your mouth!
issues.justification: Context is the dentist's patient with an open mouth; the line is confusing and unclear in English, lacking the dental context.

issues.source_quote: Ульяна Андреевна, я царствовал, но Вам не изменил! Меня царицей соблазняли
issues.translation_quote: They tempted me with a Tsaritsa
issues.justification: Minor: 'tempted with a Tsaritsa' is awkward; 'tried to seduce me with a queen' would be natural.

issues.translation_quote: Profession de foi!
issues.justification: The French pun on Russian 'профессия' / mispronunciation of 'profession de foi' is rendered literally and does not carry the joke; the preceding line should be linked.

issues.source_quote: Берегитесь... Отведай ты из моего кубка!
issues.translation_quote: Taste thou from my goblet!
issues.justification: Inconsistent use of 'thou' forms: Ivan's speech mixes modern and archaic ('Do you drink vodka?' vs 'thou'), so the register of Ivan shifts unevenly and the subtitles feel stylized rather than naturally archaic.

issues.translation_quote: Your Honor
issues.justification: Inconsistent with other forms of address ('Your Excellency' for 'сиятельство'); 'Your Honor' suggests a judge.

issues.translation_quote: Well, hello there!
issues.justification: The Russian idiom expresses indignant surprise ('Well, I like that!'); the translation sounds like a friendly greeting.

issues.translation_quote: You've gone cross-eyed from drink!
issues.justification: 'Окосел' means 'got drunk/blotto' colloquially; 'cross-eyed' is overly literal.

issues.source_quote: Это же все же, все же, что нажито непосильным трудом
issues.translation_quote: Everything, everything I acquired through backbreaking labor
issues.justification: The phrase echoes Ilf and Petrov's 'нажито непосильным трудом' comic cliché; acceptable but flattened.

issues.translation_quote: This is some kind of dream!
issues.justification: Minor: the exclamations at the banquet in the original include 'Лепота!', 'Красота!'; rendering as 'Splendor' and 'Beauty' is clumsy for spoken dialogue.

issues.translation_quote: The floor is open to everyone!
issues.justification: Mistranslation: 'Everybody dance!' is meant; 'the floor is open' implies speaking.

issues.source_quote: Да не повторяй, а повторяй! Тихо!
issues.translation_quote: Don't say "repeat," just repeat it! Quiet!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the source gag involves 'не повторяй, а повторяй' (Ivan telling him to repeat vs. dictate); the clarity of the joke is weakened.

issues.translation_quote: I must have gotten a good knock!
issues.justification: Slightly stilted; 'I got a hell of a knock' is more natural.

issues.source_quote: Черт побери! У нас в руках был сам Милославский!
issues.translation_quote: Damn it! We had Miloslavsky himself in our hands!
issues.justification: Fine; no issue. (retracted)
